title: Uncensoring open-weight models — learning roadmap
subtitle: From transformer theory to shipping an abliterated model on HuggingFace, with a no-GPU-required practice lane.
overview: Six phases, roughly 6-12 months at serious part-time. The user-facing status below reflects a reader who knows theory through Phase 2 but has not yet practiced SFT/LoRA. Every phase lists what to learn, what to practice, how to validate, and the free videos / papers / repos / app pages that teach it.
note: Reference curriculum compiled from public research and community repos. It describes public open-source techniques (abliteration, SFT, DPO, QLoRA). Verify licenses and provider policies before applying to a specific model.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.subtitle: Prereqs you already have — bookmark for sharing with others.
phases.overview: Linear algebra, PyTorch, numeric formats. Load-bearing bits for later: SVD and rank (for weight projection in Phase 4), broadcasting (for activation hooks in Phase 3), and quantization math (so you understand why int4 QLoRA works).

learn.detail: matmul, SVD, eigenvectors, rank, projections. The projection formula is the one you'll use in Phase 4 abliteration.
tensors, autograd, nn.Module, forward hooks, device management. Hooks are how you'll grab residual-stream activations in Phase 3.
fp32 / bf16 / fp16 / fp8 / int8 / int4. Understand why QLoRA's nf4 beats naive int4.

practice.how: Write it from scratch in <50 lines of PyTorch. No nn.MultiheadAttention. Test it against the built-in on random inputs.
practice.validate: Max absolute diff vs nn.MultiheadAttention under 1e-5 on fp32.

practice.how: Follow Karpathy's makemore+nanoGPT until the loss goes under 1.5 on 2M parameters.
practice.validate: Can generate a 200-char sample that is recognisable English.

prompts.title: Linalg tutor prompt
prompts.purpose: Drill projections and SVD until automatic
prompts.text: Act as my linear algebra tutor. I need the projection formula and SVD to be automatic for mechanistic interpretability work. Every message, (1) pose one short conceptual question, (2) give me a tiny numeric problem to solve on paper (3-4 numbers max), (3) wait for my answer and grade it strictly. Start with: what does it mean geometrically to project vector v onto the direction d?

phases.title: Transformer internals
phases.subtitle: Theory you have — now re-ground it in code you can poke.
phases.overview: The residual-stream model of a transformer is the mental model for every subsequent phase. If you can't draw which matrix reads from / writes to the residual stream, abliteration in Phase 4 will feel like black magic. Fix that here.

learn.detail: Every layer reads the residual, writes a delta, passes it on. Attention heads and MLPs are the two write-sources. This is Anthropic's 2021 framework.
Q, K, V projections; attention patterns as read operations; induction heads as a canonical example of a learned circuit.
Geva et al. 2021: W_up acts as keys, W_down acts as values. The MLP is a soft dictionary lookup.
Pre-norm vs post-norm, RoPE vs learned positional, GQA (grouped-query attention), MoE routing.
`I cannot` is often two tokens, not one — matters when you measure per-token refusal probability in Phase 3.

practice.task: Load Llama-3-8B, print residual stream per layer
practice.how: Use `transformer_lens.HookedTransformer.from_pretrained('meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct')`. Forward the string 'I cannot help with that'. Print the residual norm at each layer.
practice.validate: You see a norm spike around layers 10-20 — that's refusal activation building.

practice.how: Use TransformerLens hook_fn to swap layer-12 residual from a refusal prompt into the forward pass of a benign prompt.
practice.validate: The benign prompt now produces refusal text — proof that the refusal direction lives in the residual, not in the weights.

phases.title: Fine-tuning fundamentals
phases.subtitle: Theory known. This is where you start practicing. Your next 4-6 weeks live here.
phases.overview: You know SFT, LoRA, DPO on paper. Running them is a different skill: chat templates, dataset formatting, trainer configs, learning-rate schedules, gradient accumulation. All of it is free-tier doable on Colab/Kaggle with QLoRA on 7-8B models.

learn.detail: Just causal-LM loss on completions. The subtleties are in the data: chat templates, masking the user turn from the loss, handling long sequences.
Hu et al. 2021 for LoRA, Dettmers 2023 for QLoRA. Low-rank adapters train 0.1-1% of parameters at 10-100x less VRAM. Nf4 quantization makes 7B fit in 6-8 GB.
Reward-free preference optimization. DPO is the one to learn first; ORPO rolls SFT and DPO into one loss and is popular in 2026.
ShareGPT, Alpaca, ChatML. The chat_template.jinja on the model's tokenizer repo is the ground truth — not the model card text.

practice.how: On Colab free (T4 16GB). Use `unsloth` for speed. Dataset: `tatsu-lab/alpaca` or `databricks-dolly-15k`. 1 epoch. Target: loss curve monotonically down, output still coherent on a held-out prompt.
practice.validate: Save adapter to Drive. Reload, sample 5 held-out prompts, eyeball coherence. Compare to base model answers on the same prompts.

practice.how: Kaggle free notebook with 2x T4 or P100. Same recipe, bigger model. Expect ~2 hours training per epoch on Alpaca-sized data.
practice.validate: Adapter runs; inference still coherent; loss drops ~0.3-0.5 over 1 epoch.

practice.how: Dataset: `unalignment/toxic-dpo-v0.2` or `cognitivecomputations/dolphin` mixed 5% with general instruction data. Same QLoRA recipe.
practice.validate: Refusal rate on AdvBench (50 prompts) drops from ~95% to <40%. MMLU retention within 2 points.

practice.how: HuggingFace TRL's `DPOTrainer`. Chosen = direct answer, rejected = refusal. 500 pairs is enough to see the effect.
practice.validate: Refusal rate drops further vs the SFT-only run; capability holds.

phases.title: Mechanistic interpretability
phases.subtitle: The branch that turns 'fine-tuning' into 'surgery'. Everything in Phase 4 depends on this.
phases.overview: Concepts live as directions in activation space (linear representation hypothesis). Refusal is one such direction. Finding it and projecting it out is the whole abliteration playbook. Learn probing, activation patching, and SAEs — in that order of priority.

learn.detail: A concept (truth, refusal, sentiment) can often be captured as a single direction in residual-stream space. The 'single direction' paper (Arditi 2024) is the operational proof for refusal.
Train a linear classifier on hidden states to detect a concept. For refusal: logistic regression on residual activations, label = 'does the model refuse this prompt'.

learn.topic: Activation patching, path patching, attribution patching
learn.detail: The toolkit for locating which component (head, MLP, layer) causally matters for a behavior. TransformerLens-native.
Decompose residual activations into monosemantic features. Anthropic 2023-2024 papers. Overkill for abliteration but essential for understanding what you broke.

practice.task: Replicate 'Refusal is Mediated by a Single Direction' on Llama-3-8B
practice.how: (1) Collect 100 AdvBench prompts + 100 Alpaca prompts. (2) Run both through Llama-3-8B-Instruct via TransformerLens, grab residual at every layer. (3) Compute `refusal_dir[layer] = mean(adv_acts[layer]) - mean(alpaca_acts[layer])`. (4) Find the layer where cosine similarity between refusal_dir and new unseen prompts separates cleanest. (5) Project the direction out of activations at inference time and re-generate.
practice.validate: On 50 held-out harmful prompts: refusal rate drops from ~90% to <20%. On 50 Alpaca prompts: coherence preserved.

practice.task: Activation-patch a refusal onto a benign prompt
practice.how: Use TransformerLens hook_fn. Forward a refusal prompt, cache residual at layer 14. Forward a benign prompt, replace its layer-14 residual with the cached one.
practice.validate: The benign prompt's completion flips to refusal language. Confirms the direction is causal, not just correlated.

practice.task: Train a linear probe for refusal
practice.how: sklearn LogisticRegression on hidden states from your 200-prompt dataset. One probe per layer; plot accuracy vs layer.
practice.validate: Accuracy peaks mid-model (typically layers 10-20 on an 8B). This gives you the correct layer for abliteration.

prompts.title: Probe design critic
prompts.text: Review my linear probe design for detecting 'this prompt will be refused' on Llama-3-8B residuals. Spot: data leakage, class imbalance, wrong layer, insufficient regularisation, representation-vs-label confound. My setup: {PASTE}. Give 3 ranked critiques and a 1-line fix for each.

phases.title: Uncensoring methods proper
phases.subtitle: The destination. Four composable techniques.
phases.overview: Abliteration (weight surgery), SFT uncensoring (data), DPO uncensoring (preferences), and composite pipelines (all three). Ship the weakest version first — a working 8B abliterated model — then compose upward. Every published uncensored release on HF uses some combination of these four.

learn.detail: Phase 3's inference-time projection baked into the weights. For each W that writes to residual: W_new = W - dir @ (dir.T @ W). No inference overhead.
Dataset-based. Train on examples of the model already complying. Mix 1-5% uncensored with 95%+ general to avoid capability collapse.
Build preference pairs with (direct answer, refusal) and flip the sign. Stronger than SFT because it directly targets the behavior.
The dolphin/nous-hermes-uncensored/abliterated-v3 releases use: base → abliterate → SFT on mixed data → DPO on preference pairs. Each step compensates for the last step's weaknesses.
Refusal rate on AdvBench + capability retention on MMLU/HellaSwag/GSM8K + coherence eyeball. All three are necessary.

practice.how: Fork Labonne's abliteration notebook. Run end-to-end on the 3B model (fits in T4 free tier). Save weights to HF.
practice.validate: Refusal rate on 50 AdvBench prompts drops below 10%. MMLU degradation under 3 points.

practice.how: Same recipe, bigger model. ~2 hours on a Kaggle P100. The refusal direction may live at a different layer; re-probe (Phase 3 step 3) first.
practice.validate: Same thresholds as above.

practice.how: QLoRA SFT your abliterated 8B on 2-5k rows of high-quality instruction data (`HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` subset). 1 epoch.
practice.validate: MMLU returns to within 1-2 points of base. Refusal rate stays low.

practice.how: DPOTrainer on ~500 `(prompt, direct_answer, refusal)` pairs. 1 epoch. Learning rate 5e-7 (DPO is hyperparameter-sensitive).
practice.validate: On a held-out AdvBench subset: refusal rate < 3%, coherence preserved. Ship this model to HF as your first real release.

practice.how: Benchmark your pipeline output against `cognitivecomputations/dolphin-2.9-llama3-8b`, `mlabonne/Llama-3-8B-Instruct-abliterated-v3`, `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B` on your own AdvBench + MMLU subset.
practice.validate: You understand *why* yours scores where it does — not just whether it's better or worse.

learn.detail: FSDP (PyTorch), DeepSpeed ZeRO stages 1/2/3, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, sequence parallelism. For QLoRA on big models, FSDP-QLoRA (Answer.AI 2024) is the frontier for consumer multi-GPU.
HQQ, AQLM, SpQR, BitsAndBytes nf4. Most matter at inference; HQQ matters at both.
vLLM, TGI, sglang, exllamav2. vLLM is the default; sglang is faster on reasoning workloads.
Gradient checkpointing, CPU offload, NVMe offload. All available in accelerate/DeepSpeed configs.

prompts.title: Model card drafter
prompts.purpose: A card that passes community review, not one that just exists
prompts.text: Draft a HuggingFace model card for my {MODEL_NAME} ({METHOD on BASE}). Include: (1) YAML header with correct tags and license inherited from the base, (2) overview paragraph, (3) method section with specific steps and hyperparameters, (4) eval table (AdvBench refusal, MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM8K vs base + 2 comparable public models), (5) usage snippet in transformers, (6) known failure modes section, (7) citations. Base model: {NAME}. Method: {SUMMARY}. My eval numbers: {TABLE}. Be direct, no hedging, no closing disclaimers beyond what HF policy requires.

fastest_path.title: The 30-day free-compute path
fastest_path.subtitle: If you want a working 8B uncensored model on HuggingFace in a month, skip the depth and do only these:

steps.task: Karpathy 'Let's build GPT' video, code along
steps.output: A working nanoGPT on your laptop (CPU is fine for toy scale)

steps.task: Labonne's QLoRA Llama-3 notebook on Colab free T4
steps.output: Your first adapter; saved to HF

steps.task: Arditi et al. paper + Labonne's abliteration notebook on Colab free T4 (3B model)
Scale to 8B on Kaggle (P100), add SFT recovery step, write the model card, push to HF

fastest_path.note: This path skips Phase 3 depth and Phase 5 entirely. You'll ship a model but not understand why it works. That's fine for a first release — do Phase 3 properly for the second.
